title: Ahead
hookLine: a teacher, a sangha, a retreat, a reading list, a vow: the path goes on
tomorrow: what did the Buddha do on the night everything changed?

cards: Between two sala trees at Kusinara, lying on his right side, the Buddha was dying. It was his last night, and the monks had gathered close.
The trees, the sutta says, flowered out of season, and the petals drifted down onto his body. Then a wanderer named Subhadda came, asking to see him. Ananda turned him away: the Teacher is weary.
Subhadda asked again. Again, no. He asked a third time.

teach.b: The Buddha heard, and said: let him come. He asks to understand, not to trouble me. Subhadda asks, listens, and becomes the last disciple the Buddha received himself.
Then the Buddha turns to Ananda with what comes after. Some of you may think: the word of the teacher is over; we have no teacher now. Don't see it that way.
The teaching and the discipline I've given you, after I'm gone, let them be your teacher. He named no one to take his place.

Earlier in the same sutta he had told Ananda he never thought of the sangha as depending on him, or of himself as the one who must lead it. The dhamma teaches, and the sangha keeps it alive between people.

teach.h: A TEACHER, A SANGHA, A VOW.
teach.b: So the path goes on in ordinary shapes: a teacher who has walked further, a sangha to sit with, a retreat, a shelf of suttas, the precepts taken again as a vow.
Then he asked the monks, three times, whether anyone had a doubt left. No one spoke.
And his last words, in Rhys Davids' translation: "Decay is inherent in all component things! Work out your salvation with diligence!"
The Pali under diligence is appamada: not letting up, staying awake. His last words weren't, it's over. They were, keep going.

how: After learning the basics, Buddhists often look for a teacher and a sangha to practice with, go on retreats, keep reading the suttas, and take or renew the precepts, sometimes as a formal vow at a temple.

o: the path past the summit, with the teaching as teacher
a promotion to teacher once five years are complete
the next life, which a Buddhist plans for in advance

games.q: the last night — tap the pairs.
p: the last disciple the Buddha received himself
turned the wanderer away three times

s: the Buddha named a successor to lead after him
he named no one. the teaching and the discipline he gave would be the teacher.
on his last night the Buddha still welcomed a newcomer
he told Ananda to let Subhadda come, and taught him.
his last words told the monks they could rest now
his last words were the opposite: work out your salvation with diligence.

games.q: your meditation group's leader moves away, and the group stops sitting until someone can be named the new master. using the Buddha's last night, what fits?
o: keep sitting together with the teaching as teacher; the group keeps it alive.
wait until a successor is named; without a master the teaching can't go on.
split up and sit alone; once the leader leaves, a group has no point.
games.why: the Buddha named no successor. the teaching and the discipline would be the teacher, and the sangha keeps it alive between people.

practice: Stand and take three slow steps, feeling each one: the heel lifting, the foot moving, the foot coming down.
Then sit, pick up a pen, and write one step for the year ahead on this path: a teacher to look for, a sangha to visit, a retreat, a book, a vow. One step, in your own hand.

wordCard.voice: Ahead: the path past the summit, with the dhamma as teacher and diligence, appamada, for the walking.

orig.note: Pali: appamada, diligence, heedfulness; in the Buddha's last words.

carryVoice: For the road: the path goes on, one step at a time, with the teaching as your teacher. Twelve of fourteen, done.
